name: Google Drive
summary: Google's file storage for personal accounts and Workspace teams, shared with Gmail and Photos quota.

factors: Google-format documents are links, not files, until they are converted
Folders shared with you depend on other people's accounts and can vanish
Sharing links embedded in years of emails and documents will break
Storage quota is pooled with Gmail and Photos

export.summary: Ordinary files copy out unchanged. Google-format documents are converted on the way, and anything you do not own needs copying first.

methods.name: Google Takeout
methods.detail: Exports your whole Drive as a set of archives, converting Google documents to the formats you choose.

methods.name: rclone
methods.detail: Copies a Drive or a shared drive directly to another cloud or server, converting Google documents as it goes. Resumable, and it copes with rate limits.

methods.name: Drive for desktop
methods.detail: Switch to 'Mirror files' so that everything is stored locally, then copy the folder. Google-format documents still arrive as link files, so convert those with Takeout or rclone.

caveats: Files in 'Shared with me' are not exported unless you make your own copies
Several files can share one name in the same Drive folder; they are renamed on export
Sharing permissions and version history do not come along
Workspace administrators should export shared drives separately; they belong to the organisation, not to a user

paths.verdict: The like-for-like replacement, and with an office editor attached it covers Docs-style editing in the browser as well.

import.summary: Use rclone to copy from Drive straight to Nextcloud over WebDAV, converting Google documents on the way, or unpack a Takeout archive into the sync folder.

transfers: Google documents, converted to open or Office formats
Access from desktop, web and phone
lost: Files that were only shared with you
Drive's search inside images and scans

paths.verdict: Choose it for large volumes or huge numbers of files where sync speed matters most.

import.summary: Create libraries that mirror your top-level folders, then copy with rclone from Drive to Seafile, converting Google documents on the way.

transfers: Google documents, converted to open or Office formats
Access from desktop, web and phone
lost: Files that were only shared with you
The surrounding apps that Nextcloud would give you

paths.verdict: For one person or a household that only needs the same folders on several computers. It is not a cloud drive.

import.summary: Download and unpack a Takeout export on one computer, share the folder in Syncthing and pair your other devices.

lost: Sharing with people outside your own devices
A proper mobile experience on iOS

paths.verdict: A lighter, files-only alternative to Nextcloud. Young, so better suited to teams happy to be early than to ones that need a long track record.

import.summary: Use rclone to copy from Drive over WebDAV, converting Google documents on the way, or unpack a Takeout archive into the desktop client's sync folder. Recreate shares afterwards.

transfers: Google documents, converted to open or Office formats
